svg.desc: candidate number: 8; slug: judgment-recovery; title: Judgment Recovery; category: Recovery services; production stage: approved_master; scores: revenue potential: 20; profit margin potential: 21; team efficiency: 16; startup accessibility: 10; automation potential: 10; dimension max: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 25; team efficiency: 20; startup accessibility: 15; automation potential: 15; total score: 77; tier label: High-Leverage Operator Play; evidence confidence: High; uncertainty band: ±3 pts; uncertainty bounds: low: 74; high: 80; uncertainty note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.; score rationale: revenue potential: Revenue Potential: 20/25. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.; profit margin potential: Profit Margin Potential: 21/25. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.; team efficiency: Team Efficiency: 16/20. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.; startup accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 10/15. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.; automation potential: Automation Potential: 10/15. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.; economics: gross revenue range: $60,000–$500,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 20–40%; owner net profit potential: $12,000–$200,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $10,000–$75,000 USD; monthly opex range: $2,000–$12,000 USD; time to first deal: 6–24 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data; scenarios: conservative: annual gross revenue usd: 60000; net profit margin pct: 20; annual owner net profit usd: 12000; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; base case: annual gross revenue usd: 280000.0; net profit margin pct: 30.0; annual owner net profit usd: 84000; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; scaled small team: annual gross revenue usd: 500000; net profit margin pct: 40; annual owner net profit usd: 200000; full time including owner: 2; contractors: 4; total people: 6; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Court deadline tracking; Payment reconciliation; key risks: Insolvent debtors; Bankruptcy stays; Enforcement costs; regulatory notes: Check collection licensing, consumer-debt rules, exemptions and lawful data access.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: distressed_asset_recovery; track id: track_1; name: Distressed Asset Recovery; mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.; inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers; Unclaimed property & judgment dockets; Surplus auction manifests; workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances; Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value; Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts; metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case; Claim approval rate; Days from filing to disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; id: b2b_class_action_contingency_recovery; track id: track_1; name: B2B Class-Action & Antitrust Settlement Contingency Recovery; mechanism: Monitor multibillion-dollar corporate antitrust and commercial class-action settlement funds (payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, SaaS) where 85–90% of eligible small businesses never file, and recover verified payouts on a 25–33% contingency fee.; inputs: Active federal B2B class-action settlement docket calendar & claims-administrator portals; B2B merchant-processing, fleet, & vendor spend intake pipeline; Contingency claim-preparation & court-authorized third-party filing agreements; workflow: Track open and upcoming commercial class-action settlements with verified court-appointed claims administrators and $50M–$5B+ settlement pools; Sign zero-upfront-cost (25–33% contingency) authorization agreements with operating restaurants, medical practices, retailers, and fleets; Extract historical merchant statements or vendor invoices, submit audited claim packages to the settlement administrator, and reconcile fee splits upon disbursement; metrics: Average gross settlement recovery per enrolled business ($5,000–$150,000+); Claim acceptance rate by court-appointed administrator (%); Net contingency fee per operator hour invested; platform risks: failure mode: Claim rejection, administrator audit hold, or court cap on third-party filer fees; trigger: Submitting unsubstantiated spend estimates, missing court bar dates, or failing to include required third-party filer disclosures; impact: Delayed payout disbursement or court-mandated fee reduction; detection metric: Deficiency-notice rate (<2% target) and 100% court-approved disclosure compliance; fallback: File strictly for verified operating businesses with primary processor/vendor statements and use court-approved third-party claim-filing riders; id: arizona_abs_mass_tort_cocounsel; track id: track_1; name: Arizona ABS Law-Firm Ownership & Survivor/Mass-Tort Co-Counsel Arbitrage; mechanism: Leverage Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1(c) and ACJA § 7-209 (which abolished ABA Rule 5.4 in Arizona via Alternative Business Structure [ABS] licensing) so non-lawyer acquisition operators can legally own an Arizona law firm, acquire inbound institutional sexual assault survivor claims (juvenile detention facilities, rideshare MDLs, clergy/boarding-school/medical lookback windows) and catastrophic mass torts, and participate in lawful co-counsel contingency fee splits ($50k–$400k+ per settled case) instead of capped flat marketing fees.; inputs: Arizona Supreme Court ABS license + designated Compliance Lawyer (ACJA § 7-209); Trauma-informed inbound acquisition funnels for state sexual-assault lookback windows & federal MDLs; 24/7 HIPAA-compliant survivor intake, facility/ride-receipt verification, & national trial co-counsel network; workflow: Form or partner with a licensed Arizona ABS law firm with an appointed Arizona-bar Compliance Lawyer to legally bridge digital acquisition and legal representation; Run empathetic, 100% inbound survivor-advocacy campaigns across open statutory lookback windows (juvenile detention centers, Uber/Lyft rideshare MDL 3084, institutional/youth-facility abuse); Execute trauma-informed intake, verify facility/detention/rideshare records, and co-counsel with specialized trial litigators under Rule 1.5(e) joint-responsibility agreements to share in back-end settlement fees; metrics: Cost per signed & record-verified survivor retainer ($1,200–$3,500 media cost); Facility/rideshare corroboration pass rate (%) & zero-fraud docket quality; Realized co-counsel contingency fee per settled case ($50,000–$400,000+ vs. $3k lead sale); platform risks: failure mode: Cross-jurisdictional Rule 5.4 fee-splitting challenges, MDL claimant-fraud rejections, or 24–48 month settlement lockup; trigger: Splitting fees in non-ABS jurisdictions without genuine legal services/joint responsibility by ABS attorneys, accepting unverified lead-brokered retainers, or undercapitalizing multi-year MDL hold times; impact: Disallowance of co-counsel fee division in restrictive states, court dismissal of uncorroborated claims, or working-capital exhaustion before settlement payout; detection metric: 100% primary-record corroboration rate (detention/medical/ride logs) and state-by-state Rule 1.5(e)/5.4 ethics opinion sign-off; fallback: Ensure licensed ABS attorneys perform substantive legal intake/case-work or pair with an MSO (Management Services Organization) structure in restrictive states, enforce strict primary-document verification before filing, and blend fast-settling single-event injury cases with multi-year institutional dockets; id: unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery; mechanism: Ingest state controller/treasury escheatment ledgers and uncashed municipal/corporate warrant registries above $25,000, cross-match corporate officers via Secretary of State filings, and execute statutory recovery agreements for a 10–25% contingent finder fee.; inputs: State controller/treasury escheatment bulk ledgers; Uncashed municipal warrant & vendor-credit registries; Secretary of State officer & FEIN cross-match index; workflow: Filter state unclaimed-property and uncashed-warrant ledgers for high-value corporate and estate accounts exceeding $25,000; Resolve active corporate officers, successor entities, or authorized fiduciaries via SOS and skip-trace databases; Execute state-compliant finder agreements with statutory fee caps and submit notarized claim packages to the treasury administrator; metrics: Average gross warrant/escheatment claim size ($25k+); Treasury claim approval rate (%); Days from notarized filing to state disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection; trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows; impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty; detection metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate; fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free; id: ucc1_expiration_refi_trigger_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: UCC-1 Filing, MCA Stacking & Maturity-Date Trigger Arbitrage; mechanism: Monitor state Secretary of State UCC-1 financing statements and continuation filings to identify operating businesses 4–9 months into high-cost Merchant Cash Advances (MCAs) or equipment notes, triggering refinance and debt-consolidation live transfers.; inputs: Daily state SOS UCC-1 initial, amendment, & termination bulk feeds; Secured-party lender dictionary (identifying MCA vs. bank/SBA filings); Live-transfer commercial refinance & SBA consolidation desk; workflow: Classify daily UCC-1 filings by secured party to isolate businesses that took high-cost short-term working capital 120–240 days ago; Enrich business owner direct phone and email and score by industry revenue stability; Contact merchants during peak renewal/payoff windows to offer lower-rate term consolidation or equipment refinancing, monetizing via broker points or live-transfer fees; metrics: UCC-to-verified-decision-maker match rate (%); Live-transfer qualification rate (%); Origination commission / referral fee per funded refi; platform risks: failure mode: TCPA automated-calling liability or state commercial-financing disclosure violations; trigger: Robocalling cell phones without consent or quoting misleading APRs in states with commercial Truth-in-Lending laws (CA, NY, UT, VA); impact: Statutory TCPA demand letters or state DFPI regulatory enforcement; detection metric: 100% DNC/litigator-scrub pass rate and statutory APR disclosure audit in regulated states; fallback: Use direct mail, B2B work-email sequences, and manual human-dialed outreach paired with compliant state commercial financing disclosures; id: hospital_lien_medical_receivables_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery; mechanism: Partner with surgical centers, air/ground ambulance operators, and specialty clinics to ingest underpaid or denied commercial insurance claims, automating federal No Surprises Act IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) and ERISA administrative appeals on a 20–35% contingency fee.; inputs: Provider 835/837 EDI remittance & denial feeds (CO-45, CO-50, PR-96 codes); Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) & regional FAIR Health benchmark database; Automated ERISA plan-document demand & Federal IDR portal filing workflow; workflow: Ingest denied and severely underpaid out-of-network commercial claims from specialty medical practices; Cross-reference payer remittances against statutory Open Negotiation windows (30 business days) under the No Surprises Act and ERISA SPD timelines; Generate evidence-backed arbitration briefs and ERISA appeals, collecting 20–35% of the incremental insurer payout above the initial remittance; metrics: Average incremental recovery per arbitrated claim ($1,500–$25,000+); IDR / ERISA appeal win rate vs. initial payer offer (%); Contingency revenue per practice partner per month; platform risks: failure mode: Missed 30-day Open Negotiation / 4-day IDR initiation statutory deadlines or HIPAA breach; trigger: Failing to file within strict federal No Surprises Act business-day windows or handling PHI without a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA); impact: Permanent forfeiture of IDR arbitration eligibility on expired claims or HIPAA compliance penalties; detection metric: 100% BAA execution before EDI ingestion and automated T-minus-5-day statutory deadline alerts; fallback: Enforce HIPAA-compliant encrypted EDI pipelines with signed BAAs and fall back to longer-window ERISA administrative appeals when IDR windows have lapsed; id: transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication; track id: track_1; name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic); mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.; inputs: State film-office production certifications, National Park Service Part 2/3 Historic Preservation filings, and utility solar/biogas/storage interconnection queues; IRS Energy Credits Online pre-filing registration verification and tax-credit recapture insurance underwriting partners; Outbound network of CPA managing partners, corporate tax directors, and family-office CIOs with $1M–$50M+ in quarterly federal/state tax liabilities; workflow: Monitor public project registries to identify middle-market solar, RNG, battery storage, independent film, and historic-rehab developers holding $1M–$25M in newly generated transferable credits; Lock up exclusive purchase or placement options at $0.83–$0.89 per $1.00 of credit prior to quarterly corporate estimated tax deadlines (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15); Package the credits with a third-party CPA cost-segregation/eligibility opinion and tax-credit recapture insurance policy; Execute a simultaneous bilateral escrow closing with a corporate taxpayer at $0.92–$0.95 on the dollar—saving the buyer 5–8% guaranteed on their tax bill while capturing a 400–800 bps riskless spread ($40k–$80k per $1M block); metrics: Face value of tax credits placed per quarter ($5M–$100M+); Net retained principal/brokerage spread (400–800 bps) per closed tranche; Days in escrow from developer IRS registration number issuance to wire settlement; platform risks: failure mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge; trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window; impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured; detection metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche; fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance; id: litigation_finance_mass_tort_docket_securitization; track id: track_1; name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates; mechanism: Pairing an Arizona Alternative Business Structure (ABS) or co-counsel law firm with an institutional litigation-finance credit facility to acquire, medically verify (via $6.50 HITECH patient-directed record requests), and package 1,000–25,000 retained mass-tort plaintiffs (PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, defective medical devices) at $1,200–$2,500 CAC—either flipping vetted case tranches to litigation-finance hedge funds at 2.5x–4x cost or holding for 35–40% global MDL settlement fee splits.; inputs: Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (JPML) docket analytics, FDA FAERS adverse-event spikes, and EPA contaminant zip-code maps; Arizona ABS / co-counsel retainer infrastructure with e-sign intake and automated HITECH Act (45 CFR § 164.524) medical-record retrieval engine; Non-recourse litigation-finance warehouse credit facility and MDL leadership co-counsel placement contracts; workflow: Identify emerging MDL mass torts with clear causation biomarkers (specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes + geographic/product exposure proof) and deep-pocket corporate defendants; Run hyper-targeted CTV, paid social, and public-record outbound campaigns to sign injured claimants directly onto joint co-counsel retainer agreements; Execute automated HITECH patient-directed electronic medical record (EMR) pulls at the federal statutory cap (~$6.50/record) and use LLM clinical parsers to verify qualifying diagnosis and exposure dates within 72 hours; Securitize verified, deficiency-free case tranches into litigation-finance buyout facilities at $4,500–$9,000 per vetted retainer or hold on the balance sheet for $25,000–$80,000+ gross contingency fees at MDL settlement; metrics: All-in cost per medically verified, deficiency-free retained plaintiff ($1,200–$2,500); HITECH medical-record retrieval turnaround time (hours) and clinical qualification pass rate (%); Secondary docket tranche sale multiple (2.5x–4.0x CAC) or net MDL settlement IRR; platform risks: failure mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake; trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants; impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers; detection metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL; fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders; id: hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage; mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.; inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records; Title report and statutory redemption calendar; Local counsel priority and notice opinion; workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility; 2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions; 3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline; 4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire; metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs; Capital days outstanding; Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate; platform risks: failure mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien; trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority; impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation; detection metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition; fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests; id: cipa_vppa_wiretap_pixel_settlement_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: CIPA Wiretap-Pixel & VPPA Statutory Privacy-Demand Settlement Arbitrage; mechanism: Support counsel-led evaluation of genuine tracking-related privacy claims using preserved consent and disclosure evidence; applicability, standing, and recoverable damages require individual legal review.; inputs: Client-authorized browser network captures; Timestamped consent flows and privacy notices; Counsel-reviewed standing and statutory applicability checklist; workflow: 1. Obtain client authorization and preserve ordinary-session tracking and consent evidence; 2. Have counsel assess actual disclosures, statutory coverage, standing, and limitation periods; 3. Route substantiated matters to retained counsel for proportionate notice and resolution; 4. Record outcomes, client distributions, and remediation without duplicate or fabricated claims; metrics: Counsel-validated matters per reviewed session; Net client recovery after disclosed costs; Evidence completeness and duplicate-claim rate; platform risks: failure mode: Unsupported statutory demand or evidence rejection; trigger: Missing standing, valid consent, or unreliable attribution of disclosed data; impact: Dismissal, sanctions exposure, and wasted case costs; detection metric: Counsel rejection rate by coverage and evidence defect; fallback: Close unsupported matters and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits instead; id: chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup; track id: track_1; name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups; mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.; inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register; Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents; Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall; workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices; 2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility; 3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices; 4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim; metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery; Allowed claim value versus purchased face value; Realized return and days to distribution; platform risks: failure mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion; trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims; impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss; detection metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio; fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries; id: out_of_statute_zombie_debt_portfolio_settlement; track id: track_1; name: Out-of-Statute Charged-Off Debt Portfolio & Self-Serve Tradeline Settlement Funnels; mechanism: Evaluate heavily discounted time-barred receivables for lawful voluntary resolution, separating collection limitation periods from credit-reporting limits and excluding extinguished or otherwise uncollectible obligations.; inputs: Account-level ownership and payment history; State limitation, revival, and collection-disclosure matrix; Dispute records and credit-reporting eligibility dates; workflow: 1. Validate account ownership, balances, bankruptcy status, and applicable limitation periods; 2. Obtain licensed legal review of collectibility, required notices, and payment-revival consequences; 3. Offer permitted voluntary self-service resolutions without lawsuit threats or credit-deletion promises; 4. Honor disputes and opt-outs, issue satisfaction records, and update only accurate eligible reporting; metrics: Validated legally collectible balance share; Net voluntary receipts after servicing costs; Dispute and disclosure-defect rate; platform risks: failure mode: Time-barred collection or reporting violation; trigger: Threatened litigation, unlawful revival solicitation, or re-aging of obsolete debt; impact: Enforcement, restitution, and servicing suspension; detection metric: Accounts failing legal-age checks and substantiated complaints; fallback: Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation; id: mca_ucc_stacking_default_restructure_brokerage; track id: track_2; name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage; mechanism: Use UCC filing changes to identify businesses that may need cash-flow review and consensual MCA restructuring, with verified obligations and disclosed compensation rather than encouraging undisclosed stacking.; inputs: Public UCC filings and termination records; Merchant-authorized contracts and cash-flow statements; Broker licensing rules and disclosed creditor compensation terms; workflow: 1. Treat UCC changes as outreach signals, not proof of default, and obtain merchant authorization; 2. Reconcile advances, liens, repayment pulls, covenants, and sustainable payment capacity; 3. Disclose dual-sided fees and conflicts; use independent counsel where representation would conflict; 4. Coordinate documented creditor-approved modifications and monitor actual payment relief; metrics: Net merchant payment relief after fees; Creditor-approved modification rate; Post-restructure missed-payment rate; platform risks: failure mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default; trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts; impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability; detection metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement; fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel; id: state_film_historic_brownfield_tax_credit_brokerage; track id: track_1; name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement; mechanism: Match certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts, retaining disclosed placement fees; transferability and buyer usability are state-specific and do not imply federal historic credits can be sold outright.; inputs: State agency project approvals and issued credit certificates; Transfer rules, recapture terms, and seller ownership records; Buyer state tax liabilities and escrow placement agreements; workflow: 1. Identify certified credits and verify state-specific transferability, issuance status, and remaining carryforward life; 2. Have independent advisers validate eligible costs, ownership, liens, recapture exposure, and buyer utilization limits; 3. Match approved buyers and sellers with disclosed pricing, fees, indemnities, and any available insurance exclusions; 4. Complete required agency transfer approvals and escrow settlement, then retain filing and post-close monitoring records; metrics: Certified transferable credit face value placed; Net placement fee per settled transaction; Transfer approval and escrow cycle days; platform risks: failure mode: Transfer rejected or purchased credit unusable; trigger: State rule change, certificate defect, recapture event, or buyer liability mismatch; impact: Failed closing or buyer tax shortfall and indemnity dispute; detection metric: Unresolved certificate exceptions and buyer utilization coverage; fallback: Suspend settlement under diligence contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; play name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; track id: track_1; failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; trigger: Failing to file within strict federal No Surprises Act business-day windows or handling PHI without a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA); impact: Permanent forfeiture of IDR arbitration eligibility on expired claims or HIPAA compliance penalties; detection metric: 100% BAA execution before EDI ingestion and automated T-minus-5-day statutory deadline alerts; fallback: Enforce HIPAA-compliant encrypted EDI pipelines with signed BAAs and fall back to longer-window ERISA administrative appeals when IDR windows have lapsed; play id: hospital_lien_medical_receivables_arbitrage; play name: Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery; track id: track_1; failure mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge; trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window; impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured; detection metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche; fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance; play id: transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication; play name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic); track id: track_1; failure mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake; trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants; impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers; detection metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL; fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders; play id: litigation_finance_mass_tort_docket_securitization; play name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates; track id: track_1; failure mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien; trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority; impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation; detection metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition; fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests; play id: hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage; play name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage; track id: track_1; failure mode: Unsupported statutory demand or evidence rejection; trigger: Missing standing, valid consent, or unreliable attribution of disclosed data; impact: Dismissal, sanctions exposure, and wasted case costs; detection metric: Counsel rejection rate by coverage and evidence defect; fallback: Close unsupported matters and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits instead; play id: cipa_vppa_wiretap_pixel_settlement_arbitrage; play name: CIPA Wiretap-Pixel & VPPA Statutory Privacy-Demand Settlement Arbitrage; track id: track_1; failure mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion; trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims; impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss; detection metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio; fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries; play id: chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup; play name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups; track id: track_1; failure mode: Time-barred collection or reporting violation; trigger: Threatened litigation, unlawful revival solicitation, or re-aging of obsolete debt; impact: Enforcement, restitution, and servicing suspension; detection metric: Accounts failing legal-age checks and substantiated complaints; fallback: Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation; play id: out_of_statute_zombie_debt_portfolio_settlement; play name: Out-of-Statute Charged-Off Debt Portfolio & Self-Serve Tradeline Settlement Funnels; track id: track_1; failure mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default; trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts; impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability; detection metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement; fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel; play id: mca_ucc_stacking_default_restructure_brokerage; play name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage; track id: track_2; failure mode: Transfer rejected or purchased credit unusable; trigger: State rule change, certificate defect, recapture event, or buyer liability mismatch; impact: Failed closing or buyer tax shortfall and indemnity dispute; detection metric: Unresolved certificate exceptions and buyer utilization coverage; fallback: Suspend settlement under diligence contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings; play id: state_film_historic_brownfield_tax_credit_brokerage; play name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement; track id: track_1
